title: Severe drought declared in parts of southern England
summary:
South East Water's operations director Douglas Whitfield said standpipes remained part of the company's drought plan but were unlikely to be needed.
Whitfield said South East Water, which supplies more than two million customers, said 92 repair crews were out across Sussex and Kent tackling leaks to minimise loss from the network.
Wessex Water, which supplies customers from Wimbleball, introduced its first hosepipe ban in 50 years in August and said the restrictions would remain in place for the foreseeable future.

title: 'Nowhere to escape' - Indonesians share footage of orange haze blanketing towns
summary:
A thick orange smog has descended on the Indonesian city of Palangka Raya.
Witnesses captured videos of the haze washing over the Kalimantan region not far from where wildfires continue to burn.
The ISPU air pollution index exceeded 1,200, according to data from the national environment ministry, four times higher than the "hazardous" level of 300 on Wednesday.
Toxic smog is choking millions across Indonesia, Singapore and Malaysia, with authorities partly blaming the agricultural clearing method known as "slash and burn" for compounding the intense haze.

title: Climate scientists issue a sobering diagnosis about Earth's 'vital signs'
summary:
The report, the latest in a series called the “State of the Climate,” measures 16 key markers of Earth’s climate.
Seven of these have reached “record extremes,” says report co-author Christopher Wolf, a research scientist at Terrestrial Ecosystems Research Associates.
“We are increasingly concerned about the risk of crossing climate tipping points that could lead to irreversible changes,” Wolf says.
“The climate emergency is already here, but the future is not yet determined,” Wolf says.
“We still have opportunities to avoid some of the worst outcomes through rapid emissions reductions, climate adaptation and broader societal changes.

title: New team heads to Antarctic port to save it from climate change
summary:
A new team of UK specialists is embarking on a 9,000-mile journey to Antarctica to protect a British science base threatened by climate change.
The UK Antarctic Heritage Trust (UKAHT), a Cambridge-based charity, is in its second year of a three-year mission to save Port Lockroy.
This year's team will install beams and props to help the buildings withstand increased precipitation and snow loading, as well as monitor the penguins.
The site is more than 80 years old and faces structural deterioration due to rising temperatures and extreme weather on the rapidly warming Antarctic Peninsula.
After initial assessments revealed serious structural weaknesses, last year's team prepared the site ready for this season's interventions, which UKAHT said was the charity's "biggest ever conservation season" at Port Lockroy.

title: What Should Exterior Insulation Do Beyond Thermal Performance?
summary:
Yet Exterior Insulation Finishing Systems (EIFS) are still frequently reduced to insulation thermal conductivity, thickness, external envelope U-values and regulatory compliance.
In new construction, continuous exterior insulation is automatically designed around the structure from the outset, helping to eliminate thermal bridges.
Exterior insulation systems naturally extend this philosophy because they ultimately form part of the finished façade.
For architects and designers, the art lies in creating without treating exterior insulation as a constraint on form or finish.
Its exterior insulation portfolio includes EIFS Alpha (EPS/Graphite EPS Insulation), EIFS Perma (Mineral Wool Insulation) and EIFS Nova (Phenolic Foam Insulation) alongside Direct Applied Exterior Finishing Systems (DEFS), XFS Beta (Acrylic basecoat) and XFS Delta (Cementitious basecoat), providing solutions for conventional on-site construction as well as off-site construction for both traditional and steel-frame structures.

title: Nepal floods: Why Balendra Shah wants India and China to work together in the Himalayan region
summary:
But it was his ambitious proposal to bring together regional rivals India and China, alongside Nepal, to tackle these shared threats that drew particular attention.
But can Nepal really bring the two regional giants together to confront a shared climate threat in a region where they have long been locked in bitter territorial disputes?
India and China share a disputed frontier stretching roughly 3,500km (2,175 miles), much of it across the Himalayas.
But the mountains that have long been a source of friction between the two countries are also facing an urgent climate threat.
Such disasters can sweep across national boundaries, threatening lives, infrastructure and livelihoods far downstream - making co-operation between the countries sharing the Himalayas increasingly important.
